title: Developing Camera-Based AI Algorithms to Monitor Water Quality at Water and Wastewater Utilities
objectives: Prioritize 3–5 high-value applications spanning drinking water and wastewater.
Compare camera platforms from RGB through multispectral/hyperspectral and define minimum technical requirements.
Develop/test computer-vision AI and validate camera-derived observations against conventional measurements under varying sites/lighting/weather/configurations.
Assess transferability/scalability across utilities, sites, camera types and IT infrastructure; define implementation pathways.
research_requirements: Explicitly build on and extend the RFP-cited WRF knowledge base.
Use a multi-site field demonstration across drinking-water and wastewater utilities.
Quantify algorithm performance under operational/environmental variation.
Test domain transfer / retraining needs and failure modes.
Plan research report plus knowledge-transfer outputs and technology deliverables.
cost_share_rules: Applicant contribution must be at least 33% of the WRF award requested.
Cash, applicant in-kind and qualifying third-party in-kind may be used only with source-compliant valuation/support.
Third-party support must identify exact contribution type/value and authorized commitment.
Do not count prospective or unsigned support as committed contribution.
internal_nonclaims: Potential Participants on the public grant page are interested utilities, not consent to join this proposal.
For-profit eligibility does not prove prime readiness.
This repository contains no legal certification, signature, portal credential, utility consent, or binding cost-share commitment.
